pain_points: High inbound call volume in the West Michigan market - "we get so many phone calls. We get a lot of phone calls"

Calls arriving after the pro shop has closed go unanswered, which he names as where he sees immediate value

current_solution: Club Profit for the tee sheet and booking, with no other third-party online booking tool; Nextiva as the phone system; two to three pro shop staff answering calls; the CourseRev course agent chat widget already live on the website. Speak Sport was evaluated for voice last winter and not taken up. No prepayment except for leagues and outings.

objections.trigger_quote: our course still feels like that human touch is still really important
objections.rep_response_summary: Jason Doepke said the system can be toggled on and off as the course sees fit and that courses often start with after-hours only, then reframed the trade-off: the cost of the personal touch can be a busy signal when a golfer is trying to book, and CourseRev can answer up to 50 concurrent calls.

objections.trigger_quote: that senior market, that's what I'm kind of hesitant about
objections.rep_response_summary: Jason Doepke offered to run a live call so he could hear how the AI engages, said he would be willing to say half the senior crowd would not know it is an AI, and pointed to the dashboard call logs, citing a course where a caller tried to ask the AI out on a date.

objections.trigger_quote: we're in the middle of our season now, so we're not going to switch over middle of a season
objections.rep_response_summary: The doc records no response to the seasonal timing point itself. The reply that followed addressed the human-touch half of the same answer - toggling on and off, starting after hours, and the busy-signal reframe. Later, at pricing, Jason Doepke proposed after-hours only as a starting point to build the business case and ramp from there.

objections.trigger_quote: we would have to seriously think about maybe trying to transition one of our staff members
objections.rep_response_summary: Jason Doepke said a lot of their customers are not reducing staff but repurposing them onto hospitality in the pro shop, and that they have coaches who have been through the same transition.

objections.trigger_quote: no guarantees that I'll sign it right away
objections.rep_response_summary: Jason Doepke asked how the decision gets made at the course and, on hearing that it sits with ownership, offered to jump on a quick call with the owner to walk them through it and answer questions.

open.evidence: Joined late but warm, recalling having seen Evan Denholm speak at the Glen Club near Chicago; then answered the opening question with the reasons they had not taken voice - the Speak Sport evaluation, mid-season timing, and "our course still feels like that human touch is still really important".

post_demo.evidence: After the live call, the dashboard walkthrough and the group-booking and 9-hole answers: "Okay. All right. That sounds cool. Um, I think I got what I needed. Good information." Just before the demo he had said "No, I mean I like I kind of like that idea."

at_pricing.evidence: No pushback and no enthusiasm on the $2.50 per booked and completed round model with no monthly or annual fee; his reply was "Okay. Yeah. So, um that just sparked my memory." and he moved straight to asking about a nearby course he had heard might be signing.

close.evidence: Asked for the paperwork - "That's That sounds good. You can send it over." - while capping expectations with "no guarantees that I'll sign it right away" and "I'm definitely we're interested in it", and took the shorter of the two follow-up options offered: "you can follow up next week. confidence_notes: Full Gemini notes plus a complete verbatim transcript: 557 turns, 00:40:57, 54,924 characters (content_tier rich), cached from the connector markdown export and matching the triage char_count exactly. Identity is the important finding in this record and it is resolved from the text, not guessed: Scott Lake is the GOLF COURSE, not a person. The Meet display name on every prospect turn is Scott Lake, and Gemini's summary therefore writes sentences like Scott Lake questioned and Scott Lake expressed concern as if that were a human being. The prospect's own name is Jared - Jason Doepke addresses him as such three times, once with Evan Denholm asking Jared? back - and the prospect himself uses the course name when scripting a greeting: "Hey, thank you for calling Scott Lake. This is our virtual assistant." His surname never appears, so attendees carries the given name alone. Anything downstream that reads Gemini's summary literally will attribute the prospect's words to a person called Scott Lake. Rule 8 also applies and is handled: Highland Creek is the existing client Jason Doepke dials for the demo, not the prospect. This is an upsell, not a cold prospect: the course already runs the CourseRev chat widget and the opening question is why they did not take voice at the same time. The first roughly seven minutes of the transcript are a CourseRev-internal pre-meeting - ISP trouble, other sales calls and a Columbus Municipal RFP - and are excluded from call_path content other than being named as the pre-meeting; Sidney Overman speaks only there. Judgement calls worth knowing about. prospect_next_move on objection 1 is re_raised_later on the reading that the senior-demographic objection nine minutes later is the same underlying doubt about whether their callers will accept an AI, narrowed to the segment he says matters most to the business; a reviewer could instead score it partially_accepted and treat the two as independent. prospect_next_move is deflected on objections 2 and 4 on a consistent rule: his next coherent utterance changes topic without engaging the rep's answer - after the senior reframe he says he is reading his computer looking for more questions, and after the staffing reframe he goes straight to billing. The short fragments interleaved through the rep's turns in both stretches are overlap artifacts and were not read as responses. Objection 3 carries a null response_tactic and a null prospect_next_move because the doc shows no reply aimed at the seasonal timing point, so there is nothing for the prospect to have responded to. prospect_seniority is the enum's unknown: his title is never stated, though he sets tee sheet rates and the booking window and, asked whether he would need to talk to a GM, answered ownership. Sentiment checkpoints are stored in schema order, but the call order was open, pricing at 00:22, demo at 00:25, close at 00:38, so the 3, 3, 4, 4 chronological sequence is what makes the trajectory rising.
